marks.^: at the beginning of a line, indents one level
marks.,: a pause that does not end the sentence
marks.…: abandons or resumes a sentence, non-terminal

semaron.title: semaron encoding
intro: Semaron Kuriale is an alphabet of capital and small letters, written left to right. This encoding writes a roman spelling in its small letters, and a capital letter in its majuscule: `th`, `dh`, `kh`, `gh`, `sh`, `zh`, `ts`, `ch` and `ng` are each one letter, read left to right, so `tch` is t and `ch` and `ngh` is `ng` and h; `ny` before a vowel is one letter and anywhere else is n and the vowel i; `q` is a letter of its own; a doubled `a`, `i` or `u` is a long vowel; and `y` before a vowel is a glide. An apostrophe or hyphen after a letter writes the catch, a mark on the letter before it.

aelwythi-semaron.title: aelwythi-semaron encoding
intro: Aelwythi has its own encoding in the Semaron Kuriale hand. Coined words use the fixed Aelwythi letter groups: ch, sh, th, dh, kh, gh, zh, ts and ng have dedicated signs, and ny takes its dedicated sign before a vowel. A group is lowercase, as in ch, or initial-uppercase, as in Ch; CH and cH are illegal. The letter q has its own sign, and y is always a consonant. There are no automatic c or x substitutions.

An acute vowel writes its ordinary vowel sign followed by the non-printing stress modifier U+E0114. Stress does not change vowel sound or length. Coined words use no diaeresis or grave accent. Doubled vowels remain two written signs.

Only a period draws the pause point. Quotation marks and apostrophes draw nothing, and a hyphen writes a space. Decoding returns a conventional Roman spelling: omitted punctuation is not restored, and a hyphen reads back as a word space. Other Semaron encodings keep their own rules.

pirzath.title: pirzath encoding
intro: Pirzath is a script of letters read left to right, drawn carved in Pirzath Carved and in a hand in Pirzath Hand on the same code points. This encoding writes a roman spelling in them: a digraph such as `th` or `kh` is a single letter, and `ay` before a consonant or at the end of a word is the single letter for the diphthong.

thuravark.title: thuravark encoding
intro: Thuravark Carved is a row of straight staves for letters, numerals and a few marks, read left to right. This encoding writes a roman spelling in them: a digraph such as `th` or `kh` is a single stave, a doubled vowel is the stave twice, and a hyphen draws nothing and is written as an invisible mark.

qalezu.title: qalezu encoding
intro: Qalezu Hand is a right-to-left script with one sign for each consonant. This encoding writes a roman spelling in them: a vowel draws nothing except at the start of a word, where it draws the catch sign; elsewhere it is written as an invisible mark, so decoding restores it, and a digraph such as `kh` is a single sign.

vedyakshara.title: vedyakshara encoding
intro: Vedyakshara Classical is a left-to-right script in which each consonant carries the vowel `a`. This encoding writes a roman spelling in it: a consonant before a vowel is the bare consonant followed by that vowel's sign, a consonant elsewhere is the consonant with the cut that takes the vowel away, and `a` draws no sign of its own and is written as an invisible mark.

helonika.title: helonika encoding
intro: Helonika Book is an alphabet of capital and small letters, written left to right. This encoding writes a roman spelling in its small letters, and a capital letter in its majuscule: `ei` and `ou` are the single letters for the long vowels, while `kh`, `zh` and doubled vowels are written as two letters.

helonika-bizarian.title: helonika-bizarian encoding
intro: A second roman spelling for Helonika Book. Here `kh` and `zh` are single letters, a doubled `a`, `i` or `u` is a long vowel, `ei` is two letters, and an acute vowel is the vowel followed by the accent mark. A capital letter is written in its majuscule.

helonika-bethuan.title: helonika-bethuan encoding
intro: A third roman spelling for Helonika Book. Here `kh` is a single letter and `zh` two, a doubled `a`, `i` or `u` is a long vowel, `ei` is the single letter for the long vowel, and an acute vowel is the vowel followed by the accent mark. A capital letter is written in its majuscule.

veldikko.title: veldikko encoding
intro: Veldikko is a right-to-left calligraphy whose letters join along the line, with vowel marks that float above them. This encoding writes a roman spelling in its code points: a letter, then the doubling bar if the consonant is doubled, then each vowel mark followed by its signs of length, pitch and emphasis.
structure: Its rows are generated from a small number of parts, so the complete table is too long to read. Every consonant is a single letter; a roman letter the script lacks (`b`, `f`, `w`, `z`, `c`, `q`, `g`) is written as the nearest letter, and `x` is written as two letters. A vowel is its vowel sign, and a vowel at the start of a word is written after the carrier letter. A doubled vowel adds the long sign. The accents circumflex, caron and acute, typed on a vowel or after it, add the rise, fall and emphasis signs. A doubled consonant adds the doubling bar.
The rows below are the rows of a single character, then a few longer rows of each length.

veldikko-aelendi.title: veldikko-aelendi encoding
intro: A second roman spelling for Veldikko, with the same letters and marks. It writes the consonant digraphs such as `th`, `dh`, `kh` and `ng` as single letters.

zethu.title: zethu encoding
intro: Khelathi Zethu Glyphs is a right-to-left script of signs, set directly beside each other with nothing between them. This encoding accepts no roman letters: Khelathi words are written by the language-aware encoder, and a sign is written by its code between `⟦` and `⟧`, in the notation of the [zethu-mdc codage](zethu-mdc.md). Its word separator is empty: whitespace in roman draws nothing and writes nothing, so no output contains U+0020, and decoding gives the `⟦…⟧` codage alone.

zethu-mdc.title: zethu-mdc codage
intro: Khelathi Zethu Glyphs is a right-to-left script of signs, one sign to a word. This codage names each sign by a code, its sense in capitals, and types the format controls in the notation of the Manuel de Codage. It is reached only between `⟦` and `⟧` of the [zethu encoding](zethu.md), and encodes no text of its own.

chalish-pilam.title: chalish-pilam encoding
intro: Chalish Pilam Common is a logographic script in which each glyph records a concept. This encoding accepts no roman letters: a glyph is written by its code between `⟦` and `⟧`, in the notation of the [chalish-common codage](chalish-common.md). Its word separator is one space, an empty cell.

chalish-pilam-ceremonial.title: chalish-pilam-ceremonial encoding
intro: Chalish Pilam Ceremonial is the carved hand of Ch'alish P'ilam, a logographic script whose glyphs compose into blocks. This encoding accepts no roman letters: a glyph or a block is written by its codes between `⟦` and `⟧`, in the notation of the [chalish-ceremonial codage](chalish-ceremonial.md). Its word separator is one space, an empty block.

chalish-ceremonial.title: chalish-ceremonial codage
intro: Chalish Pilam Ceremonial is the carved hand of Ch'alish P'ilam, a logographic script whose glyphs compose into blocks. This codage names each glyph by a code: a concept glyph by its name in capitals (`SUN`), a syllable sign by its syllable and number (`ka1`), and a number by `n` and its value (`n13`). It is reached only between `⟦` and `⟧` of the [chalish-pilam-ceremonial encoding](chalish-pilam-ceremonial.md), and encodes no text of its own.

Inside a block, `*` writes the joiner that sets two items side by side and `:` the joiner that stacks the first over the second; the font lays the block out from them. A block ends wherever no joiner follows, so `-` writes only its invisible mark, and whitespace only separates codes. Zero and the places of the count have code points and no ceremonial drawing, so they print the box.

chalish-common.title: chalish-common codage
intro: Chalish Pilam Common is a logographic script in which each glyph records a concept. This codage names each glyph by a code, such as `n1` for the numeral one or `SUN` for the sun. It is reached only between `⟦` and `⟧` of the [chalish-pilam encoding](chalish-pilam.md), and encodes no text of its own.

teng-chou.title: teng-chou encoding
intro: Teng Chou is a logographic script of the Tantsou: one character for each morpheme, with a syllabary of 87 signs for particles, verb endings and island words. Its characters are set directly beside each other, with nothing between them. This encoding accepts no roman letters: Tantsou words are turned into characters by the language-aware encoder, and a character is written by its code between `⟦` and `⟧`, in the notation of the [teng-chou-codes codage](teng-chou-codes.md). Its word separator is empty: whitespace in roman draws nothing and writes nothing, so no output contains U+0020.

teng-chou-codes.title: teng-chou-codes codage
intro: Teng Chou is a logographic script of the Tantsou. This codage names each character by a code: a character by its morpheme in capitals (`WONG`), a stage of the tally by `TALLY1` to `TALLY5`, and a sign of the Jurthati syllabary by its syllable in lowercase (`ka`). Case separates a character from a sign that shares its spelling, so `KA` and `ka` are different characters. It is reached only between `⟦` and `⟧` of the [teng-chou encoding](teng-chou.md), and encodes no text of its own.
